items.title: Polisar – kompakte Pads, großer Stationskern
items.description: Station an der oberen Kartengrenze: senkrechte Tragringe, kompakte aufgeteilte Pads, größerer Innenbereich mit blauer Kugel und zwei Großschiff-Dockingports.
items.prompt:
Use case: compositing / style-transfer. Create a revised polished gameplay visual target by REBUILDING the native game station in IMAGE 1, informed by the physical ring orientation in IMAGE 2 and ONLY the detailed industrial surface rendering quality of IMAGE 3.
INPUT ROLES: Image 1 is the actual native game station layout to preserve and improve: roofless central blue-globe room, surrounding shops, two medium front-left pads, one larger front-center pad, four small front-right pads in a 2 by 2 group. Image 2 is the user's real Port Olisar TOP VIEW: a long horizontal x-axis spine and UPRIGHT rings, whose planes are PERPENDICULAR to the horizontal play plane. Image 3 is the previous generated art: use ONLY its beautiful detailed off-white/gray/yellow metal materials, fine machinery, black space, UI and regular hexes; its flat circular ring orientation and massive width are WRONG and MUST NOT be copied.
GAMEPLAY COMPOSITION: One single 16:9 landscape image, a zoomed near-top-down orthographic MAP VIEWPORT, yaw nearly zero, pitch about 68 degrees, no perspective vanishing point. The whole local map is 512 by 256 hexes; show a crop near its upper edge. The playable map fills the image BELOW a clearly visible thin straight horizontal boundary about 18 percent down from the top of the image. The station lies astride this boundary. The boundary passes just BEHIND the main horizontal station axis and rear wall of the front rooms, leaving ALL rooms of the front campus inside the playable area. The station's rear half continues above that boundary as dim non-playable exterior decoration cropped by the top image edge. No grid above boundary; uninterrupted consistent hex grid EVERYWHERE below boundary, including empty space. In the lower 55-60 percent of the frame there is mostly open black hex-space for approach.
STATION GEOMETRY: Compact the native station, keeping its readable split pad arrangement. Make all the exposed landing pads about 40 percent SMALLER relative to the central rooms. Enlarge the central roof-cutaway room and surrounding interior/shop rooms about 35 percent, with a broader spacious interior floor plan. The central room has the small glowing BLUE HOLOGRAPHIC SPHERE on its pedestal; shops, benches, practical service desks, cargo equipment and tiny adult people around it. Roofs removed ONLY for gameplay interior visibility, complete walls and doorways remain. A continuous enclosed or airlock-connected circulation path reaches each actual pad. Keep two M pads front-left, one modest L pad center, four S pads front-right in a compact 2-by-2 group. Proportions should favor the rooms rather than a sprawling slab of landing decks.
RINGS: Two principal large UPRIGHT industrial truss rings flank the main room and a smaller axial ring assembly can be toward the outer end, derived from Image 2. Their axis is horizontal left-to-right. Each ring plane is vertical, perpendicular to the pad deck and game grid. From this steep overhead view they project as VERY NARROW, almost EDGE-ON vertical ellipses/strips running front-to-back in the image, with little apparent open area. Show a little visible side curve from the shallow tilt so they read as standing rings. NEVER show four face-on round circles lying flat like wheels on the map.
LARGE SHIP DOCKING: Add exactly TWO clearly distinct attached docking-port arms outside the little landing-pad clusters, one far left and one far right. Each arm has a substantial telescoping pressurized gangway, a closed docking collar and clamp assembly facing outward into clear space. Small readable labels 'Dock 1' and 'Dock 2' can distinguish these from pads. These are genuine ship-side docking connections, NOT extra giant landing pads. Keep their approach volumes unobstructed and clear of rings. No giant visiting ship is needed.
VISUALS: Rich Star Citizen-style purposeful industrial detailing, slight wear, pipes, trusses, tanks, warm worklights, muted off-white/gray/ochre. Render it as a readable illustrated game world, not a film shot. In the black approach field, one utility ship two hexes long and one LIGHT/MEDIUM fighter only ONE HEX long; the hulls should actually fit those existing grid cells. Grid cells equal size and orientation across map. No enlarged hero ships. A sparse straight approach guide points toward an actual pad. Slim title strip exact text 'POLISAR · STATIONSANFLUG'; tiny navigator '512 × 256'. Small boundary annotation 'Kartengrenze' with 'Dekoration' above and 'Spielfeld' below is acceptable. Clear layout and upright physical rings matter more than extra greebles. No planet, no ground buildings, no floating disconnected pads, no new perspective camera, no inset/collage.
